title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Flight Ground Stop After 14,500 Disruptions, Trump Sets First Trilateral Summit With Xi and Putin in China, and Indonesia Drops Commodity Export Monopoly
subhead: US flights resumed after a four-hour telecommunications outage grounded departures nationwide and prompted a $50 billion modernization demand; the White House announced an unprecedented Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit at APEC to discuss nuclear arms cuts and Iran; and Jakarta scrapped plans for a state-owned export monopoly over coal, palm oil, and ferroalloys.

sections.heading: FAA Lifts Four-Hour Nationwide Ground Stop After 14,500 Flight Disruptions
sections.body:
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday evening after a telecommunications outage across Air Route Traffic Control Centers halted all domestic departures starting at 3:44 p.m. ET—only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history, according to The Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, and CNBC. The four-hour stoppage disrupted more than 14,500 flights, including roughly 10,000 delays and 4,700 cancellations, stranding hundreds of thousands of passengers across US hubs and delaying US-bound departures from Sydney and Melbourne (Business Insider, The Guardian, CNA).

US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said overloaded legacy switches and routers failed under heavy data traffic and demanded $50 billion from Congress to overhaul aging air traffic control infrastructure, while Canadian transport officials confirmed Canada's airspace operated normally (Business Insider, NBC News, Anadolu Agency). Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated there was zero evidence of a cyberattack, and both Microsoft and FAA SMART AI vendor Air Space Intelligence confirmed their products were not responsible for the aviation halt (MarketWatch, France 24, Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: A single telecommunications failure briefly paralyzed the world's largest aviation market and exposed how aging routing hardware leaves national transport infrastructure vulnerable even without a cyberattack.

sections.heading: Trump to Hold First Trilateral Summit With Xi and Putin at APEC in China
sections.body:
The White House announced on Friday that US President Donald Trump will hold a historic first-ever trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on November 19 on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China, following an initial stop in the Philippines, according to The Hill, Bloomberg, and AFP. Senior US officials told Reuters, CNA, and Anadolu Agency that Trump plans to focus the three-way talks on nuclear arms reductions and the war in Iran rather than the Ukraine conflict, though Washington does not expect a formal agreement from the session.

Speaking ahead of the trip, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is 'no need' for further military strikes on Iran because the economic pain on Tehran is already severe, even as he defended earlier actions against Iran's nuclear program (The Times of Israel). Separately, US officials told the Financial Times and CNBC that Trump does not intend to raise the espionage scandal surrounding resigned Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang during his summit with Xi.
sections.whyItMatters: Convening the first-ever trilateral summit among Washington, Beijing, and Moscow around nuclear arms control and Iran—while keeping Ukraine and the Nvidia espionage probe off the table—marks a major shift toward direct great-power bargaining.

sections.heading: Treasury-Commerce Rift Deepens Over Nvidia's China-Linked Client Megaspeed
sections.body:
Fallout from the ouster of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang intensified in Washington as US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick for failing to ban Nvidia chip sales to Megaspeed, the Singapore-based firm formerly led by suspected Chinese intelligence intermediary Alice Huang, according to CBS News. In an exclusive report, Reuters revealed that Jensen Huang had misled Nvidia's top general counsel regarding his extramarital relationship with the Chinese businesswoman prior to his resignation, while veteran chief financial officer Colette Kress assumed the role of interim CEO.

Despite the executive upheaval and a dip in Nvidia shares, broader US equity markets held steady on Friday as Republican lawmakers pressed to question Huang before Democrats assume control of Congress in January (The New York Times, CNBC). In Asia, semiconductor analysts told CNA that the Nvidia-Megaspeed investigation is likely to trigger stricter US end-user verification rules and narrow Singapore's room to maneuver as a regional AI data center and chip distribution hub.
sections.whyItMatters: Open cabinet friction between the Treasury and Commerce secretaries over Megaspeed points to tougher enforcement against third-country semiconductor transshipment hubs in Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: Suspected Drones Trigger Alert at RAF Lakenheath as Polish President Vetoes EU Online Safety Law
sections.body:
US Air Force security forces responded on Friday evening to suspected unauthorized drone activity above RAF Lakenheath in England, marking the third drone incident near UK bases hosting American combat aircraft in recent weeks, Le Monde, The Times of Israel, and the South China Morning Post reported. Both Britain's Ministry of Defence and a USAF spokesperson subsequently confirmed that the incident was resolved and that no personnel, warplanes, or base infrastructure were affected.

Across Europe, Polish President Karol Nawrocki vetoed an EU-aligned online safety law for a second time, arguing the legislation threatens freedom of expression and deepening his standoff with Prime Minister Donald Tusk, who insisted child protection online must transcend partisan divides (Anadolu Agency). Meanwhile, leaders from all 27 EU member states convened in Dublin to debate how to balance artificial intelligence regulation, technological sovereignty, and financing rules (Le Monde).
sections.whyItMatters: Repeated drone incursions over US airbases in Britain and Warsaw's veto of EU digital rules highlight simultaneous security and regulatory strains across the European alliance.

sections.heading: Indonesia Drops State Commodity Export Monopoly and All Survive New Orleans Tanker-Cruise Crash
sections.body:
Indonesia abandoned controversial plans to designate a powerful new state-owned enterprise as the sole exporter of its palm oil, coal, and ferroalloys, opting instead to require exporters to submit comprehensive pricing and shipment data to the state, the South China Morning Post reported. The policy U-turn reassured private mining and agricultural producers across Southeast Asia, though questions remain over how Jakarta will enforce oversight and benchmark export royalties.

In the United States, more than 100 passengers and crew were accounted for in what officials called a 'miracle on the Mississippi' after a tanker lost control and collided with the docked paddlewheel river cruise liner American Heritage near the Port of New Orleans, sending 32 people to local hospitals with non-critical injuries (The Guardian, Axios, AP News, The Independent). Elsewhere, the Trump administration delayed enforcement of federal Medicaid work requirements that had been slated to take effect in January (The New York Times), while Russia ordered a cull of up to 30% of its brown bear population after fatal attacks killed 36 people this year (SCMP).
sections.whyItMatters: Jakarta's retreat from a state export monopoly preserves private commodity supply flows across Asian energy and metals markets, while shifts in US healthcare enforcement reflect domestic policy recalibrations after the midterms.

bottomLine: Friday and Saturday underscored both physical infrastructure fragility and shifting geopolitical alignments: a four-hour FAA telecommunications outage disrupted more than 14,500 US flights and sparked a $50 billion modernization push, while the White House scheduled the first-ever trilateral summit among Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin in China to address nuclear arms reductions and the Iran war. At the same time, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent clashed with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over Nvidia's sales to Singapore-based Megaspeed, US forces responded to a third suspected drone incursion at RAF Lakenheath, and Indonesia backed away from a state monopoly over coal, palm oil, and ferroalloy exports.
sources: Wall Street Journal, Financial Times, CNBC, The Guardian, Business Insider, France 24, NBC News, MarketWatch, CNA, The Hill, Bloomberg, AFP, Reuters, Times of Israel, CBS News, New York Times, Le Monde, South China Morning Post, Anadolu Agency, Axios, AP News, The Independent
